clue.text: Staff and volunteers each ringing one caller, primarily lawmen

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the word for staff goes around the one-caller letters

parts.note: a staff is a pole
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of caller is used

parts.note: a caller is a visitor; only its first letter is wanted here

indicators.note: and carries the ringing on to the word for volunteers, so it too surrounds letters

parts.note: to volunteer is to offer, so volunteers is offers
each means both words get the same pair, so the one-plus-caller letters are supplied a second time

explanation.surface: A police station's staff and volunteers each phone someone, mainly officers of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like telephoning, but means encircling; 'each' makes both words enclose the same two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawmen is an informal term for those who enforce the law, which is what constables and sergeants do.

clue.text: Key way in reproduction method where crosses accumulate

indicators.note: in means the key and the way are placed inside the reproduction method

parts.note: pollination is how flowering plants reproduce
G is a musical key
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A key route into how plants reproduce.
explanation.walkthrough: The online clue first read 'Key fact', which cannot work; the printed 'Key way' does. 'reproduction method' suggests biology, but crosses are the marks voters put on ballot papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark a cross on ballot papers at a polling station, so the crosses pile up there.

clue.text: Travelling collier, heading off round eastern rock

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the eastern letter
travelling means the letters move about into a new order
heading off means the first letter of collier is dropped

explanation.surface: A coal miner on the road, losing his head as he circles an eastern crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves OLLIER, which 'Travelling' rearranges around E. The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine, legendary home of a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a famous steep slate cliff above the Rhine in Germany, so a rock by name.

clue.text: Case confined to research establishment

indicators.note: confined to means the answer is kept within the letters of the words

explanation.surface: A legal case kept within a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large box for storing things, so it is a case or container.

clue.text: Person using drill interrupts speaker

indicators.note: interrupts means the drill letters break into the speaker word

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
PE, physical education, is drill or exercise

explanation.surface: A workman with a power drill cuts across someone speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' suggests a power tool, but it is PE, school exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works or uses a machine or system.

clue.text: Nancy's son importing American firearms

indicators.note: importing means taking the American letters inside

parts.note: fils is French for son, and Nancy is a French city

explanation.surface: A boy called Nancy brings in guns from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is the city in France, so 'Nancy's son' is French: FILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusils are old flintlock muskets, a type of firearm.

clue.text: Cons that are bound to work?

definitions.text: Cons that are bound to work?

parts.words: Cons that are bound to work?
parts.note: convicts chained together and set to labour; bound means both tied up and obliged

explanation.walkthrough: Cons that are bound to work sounds like reliable tricks, but cons are convicts and bound means shackled.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of prisoners chained together for outdoor labour.

clue.text: Sally's position in office

indicators.note: in means the position letters sit inside the office word

parts.note: an office is a religious service or rite
POS is the abbreviation for position

explanation.surface: Sally's job in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name, but it is a witty retort; office is a church service, not a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty remark, and a riposte is a quick clever reply.

clue.text: Make the locks secure and calm down!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, keep one's hair fixed in place on the head
second meaning: an idiom telling someone not to lose their temper

explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggests doors, but they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep your hair on is a British idiom urging someone to stay calm, and literally it means not losing one's hair.

clue.text: Most of silver parts reduced in size

indicators.note: the letters for silver split, or part, the word for reduced by sitting in its middle

parts.note: reduced, made smaller, gives less

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: argent is the heraldic word for silver

explanation.surface: A silver item mostly breaks into smaller pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Argent is the heraldic word for silver; 'parts' is a verb here, the silver splitting the word for reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness and size both name the dimension or bulk of a thing; synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Fruit drink without the odd bits of pip

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the drink's letters go around the others

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first and third letters of pip

explanation.surface: A fruit drink with no fragments of seed in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense outside, not lacking, so the drink wraps the picked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit; the definition names its class.

clue.text: Admit altering order for small marine arm

indicators.note: altering order means the two parts of the phrase for admit swap places

parts.note: to admit is to let in

explanation.surface: A rule change lets someone into a small branch of the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: LET IN (admit) has its two words swapped by 'altering order'. A marine arm suggests a navy, but it is an arm of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow stretch of water reaching into the land, a small arm of the sea.

clue.text: Convincingly toppled leader in seventies denied last drink

indicators.note: denied last means the final letter of the leader's name is removed

parts.note: Salvador Allende, president of Chile, was overthrown in the 1973 coup
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A deposed seventies leader is refused a final drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvador Allende was the Chilean president ousted in the 1973 coup; winning all ends up is a British idiom for winning comprehensively.
explanation.definitionFit: To win all ends up is an idiom for winning thoroughly or decisively, so the phrase means convincingly.

clue.text: Child following current affairs

indicators.note: following means the word for child comes after the word for current

parts.note: going, as in the going rate, means current
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A child keeping up with current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current affairs' reads as one phrase, the news, but current belongs to the wordplay and affairs alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are events or happenings, especially questionable ones, a sense of affairs.

clue.text: Scientist initially examining old journal, in essence

indicators.note: in means the three pieces are placed inside the word for essence

parts.note: the gist is the essence of something

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of examining

parts.note: a log is a journal or record

explanation.surface: A scientist starts by examining an old journal, in essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in essence' reads as 'basically', but it is a container: the essence word holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A geologist is a scientist who studies the earth's rocks and structure.

clue.text: Improvised panegyric mother recalled

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the letters run backwards

parts.note: a panegyric is a speech or poem of praise, as an ode is
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A tribute to a mother that someone remembered, made up on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with whatever is to hand, which is improvising.

clue.text: Bird very hot sitting on egg?

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on means the hot word is placed above the egg

parts.note: flaming means burning, very hot
O is shaped like an egg

explanation.surface: A bird in fierce heat brooding on its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: Address system in centre certain to cause bother

indicators.note: the centre of certain is its single middle letter

parts.note: to annoy is to bother someone

explanation.surface: A public address system in a building's central hall is bound to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannoy is a brand name that became the British word for any public address loudspeaker system.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tannoy is a loudspeaker public address system, so it names the address system itself.

clue.text: Return, resolved to acquire university education

indicators.note: to acquire means the rearranged letters take in the university letter
resolved means the letters of return are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes back, determined to get a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like determined, but signals that RETURN is rearranged around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture as a noun is the upbringing and training of a child, which is an education.

clue.text: Fellow bachelor carrying less weight

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
something carrying less weight is lighter

explanation.surface: A single man who has slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: A blighter is British informal for a person, usually a mildly annoying one.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is a slangy British word for a chap or man, a sense shared with fellow.

clue.text: Starts using bags, a couple wife cast out

parts.note: to bag is to take, so bags is takes

indicators.note: cast out means the wife letter is removed

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Someone takes up using bags after a couple throw out the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to something is to begin doing it as a habit.

clue.text: Third person tipped trendy vitamin

indicators.note: tipped, as in tipped over, means the name is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam and Eve, was the third person in the Bible
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A grammatically third-person subject recommends a fashionable vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third person' suggests grammar, but it is Cain, the third human after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin is vitamin B3, also called nicotinic acid.

clue.text: Flaw is found in disheartened team's intimidatory tactics

indicators.note: found in means the flaw and the word is are placed inside the other letters
disheartened means the heart, the middle letters, of team is removed

parts.note: team, with the 's read as 'has' joining it to the rest
an error is a flaw

explanation.surface: A dispirited side discovers a weakness in its own bullying play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle letters of team, leaving only its outer pair to hold the flaw and the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrorism is the use of fear and violence to coerce, intimidation as a method.

clue.text: Sound coming from furrow on the level

indicators.note: sound means the answer is said the same as the word for furrow

parts.note: to pucker is to furrow or wrinkle, as a brow does

explanation.surface: The noise made by a ploughed groove across flat ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent PUCKER sounds like PUKKA, a word from Hindi meaning genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka means genuine or authentic, and something on the level is honest and genuine.

clue.text: White House deputy turned up European bug

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the deputy word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: veep is US slang for the vice president

explanation.surface: The vice president arrived with a European insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect, but as a verb it means annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To peeve is to irritate, the same as to bug someone.

clue.text: Retro company regularly built in circular windows

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the company abbreviation is reversed
regularly means taking every other letter of built in

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned firm routinely fits round windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' turns CO into OC; 'regularly' takes the even letters U, L, I of built in.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculi, plural of oculus, are round or eye-shaped windows, as in a dome.

clue.text: Academic not for but against King Edward?

indicators.note: not marks the word for 'for' as the part to take out of the academic
but brings in the word for 'against' as the replacement

parts.note: a professor is an academic
pro means for, in favour of
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A scholar who opposes rather than supports the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Confessor was the English king who died in 1066; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward the Confessor bore the epithet, so the title stands for that monarch.

clue.text: Wearying, as today's successful solvers must be?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: getting someone down is depressing or tiring them

definitions.text: as today's successful solvers must be?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: solvers who finish are getting the clue's last entry written in

explanation.walkthrough: Getting someone down means dispiriting them; a solver also gets a down clue, and this clue's answer is itself 26, so read the second part literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting one down is an idiom for depressing or tiring a person; a solver also literally gets each down clue.
